case.background: An ideal blackbody (emissivity one) exchanges only thermal radiation with a cooler black enclosure. Determine how net radiative power depends on emitter temperature, enclosure temperature, and emitting area.
initial_observations: Net power is outward throughout the available temperature range.

controls.description: Absolute temperature of the enclosing radiative environment.
controls.name: ambient_temperature_k

instruments.description: An ideal black emitter of selectable area in a black, temperature-controlled enclosure, with a calibrated net-radiation calorimeter.
instruments.name: thermal_radiation_calorimeter

notes: This is a deterministic idealized benchmark world, not a literal replay of a historical data table.
A valid experiment changes only listed controls and consumes one episode attempt.
Emissivity is fixed at one; conduction and convection are excluded from the reported net-radiation readout.

FinalSubmission.model must equal 'net_radiation_power_law'. FinalSubmission.parameters must contain exactly reference_power_scale_w, temperature_exponent. Candidate law: P = reference_power_scale_w*(emitting_area_cm2/100)*[(emitter_temperature_k/500)^temperature_exponent - (ambient_temperature_k/500)^temperature_exponent]

readouts.description: Net radiative power leaving the emitter.
readouts.name: net_radiative_power_w

case.title: Identify the net thermal-radiation relation
